title: 2009 HMMT November Guts Problem 3
statement: Consider a square, inside which is inscribed a circle, inside which is inscribed a square, inside which is inscribed a circle, and so on, with the outermost square having side length 1. Find the difference between the sum of the areas of the squares and the sum of the areas of the circles.

solutions.text:
\(2-\frac{\pi}{2}\)

The ratio of the area of each square and the circle immediately inside it is \(\frac{4}{\pi}\). The total sum of the areas of the squares is \(1+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}+\ldots=2\). Difference in area is then \(2-2 \cdot \frac{4}{\pi}\).
\(2^{\text {nd }}\) ANNUAL HARVARD-MIT NOVEMBER TOURNAMENT, 7 NOVEMBER \(2009 —\) GUTS ROUND
